note:
# Census pass: P-E-2018-89499-90bc677f

## What the paper is
A fragility index built in three stages - Pressure-State-Response assigns the indicators,
the Entropy Weight Method weights them, Discriminant Analysis cuts the result into fragile,
vulnerable and stable bands - then instantiated twice, on Sudan and on Egypt, with a Gray
Relational Analysis of which climatic variable moves which social indicator, a linear
forecast to 2028 for Egypt, and an intervention sheet priced in dollars. Twenty-two
physical pages, eighteen printed exhibits: Figures 1 to 12 and Tables 1 to 6.

## Coverage arithmetic
Twenty-two measured regions on fourteen of the twenty-two pages. Seventeen of them are
recorded here: eleven figure rows plus six table rows. Five are excluded as
`not-an-exhibit`, and all five are equations - the min-max standardization and the
proportion formula on p8, and the entropy, variation-coefficient and weight formulas on
p9. So 17 + 5 = 22 and the region list closes.

It closes with a deficit of one. Figure 8 - the variance chart for Sudan - is drawn,
titled, captioned ('Figure 8 Variance of Stress, Status and Response Indicators in
Sudan') and pointed at ('are shown in Figure 8'), and the pass returns exactly one region
on p11, which belongs to Figure 7's plotting band. There is no bbox for Figure 8, so no
row can be recorded for it, and this paper joins the short list of censuses whose region
list lost an exhibit rather than an accounting error.

## Reading the region areas
Three chart regions are floors, not measurements. Figures 7, 10 and 12 return 0.0261,
0.0227 and 0.0118 of the page - thin bands across the plotting area only - while their
titles, axis labels and legends fall outside the box. The charts themselves occupy
roughly a quarter of a page. This is the same lesson as #168's double-boxing, pointed the
other way: a region is a box around ink, and the pass is free to box a fifth of a
drawing as long as that fifth is the only part it recognises as an image.

## Caption side and the invisible caption
Caption side splits inside the paper. All six tables print their caption ABOVE the grid;
all twelve figures print theirs BELOW the art. Two papers in this lane have already shown
that caption side is a habit rather than a law (#167 figures below and tables above,
#168 everything below); this is the first paper in the lane where one document uses both
conventions at once, split cleanly along the figure/table line.

Table 1 is the paper's trap. 'Table 1 Notations of the model' prints on p4, centred over
a two-column symbol list, and the caption string does not exist in the text layer at all:
the layer runs from the heading '2.2 Notations' straight to '3 The Model of Fragility'.
The table itself is invisible to the text layer for the same reason. It is recorded here
with `caption_source` = `typed-from-crop`, and it is the paper's only exhibit that is
never announced by any sentence - the notation section simply ends and the next section
begins.

## What the figures are made of
Twelve figures, two families, no exceptions. Figures 1 to 5 are flowcharts - boxed nodes,
blue fill, downward arrows, one per indicator layer with a fourth showing the coupling
system - and not one of them carries a legend, a number or an axis. Figures 6 to 12 are
computed charts of only two designs: stacked stress/status/response bars with the
fragility series overlaid as a line (7, 9, 11, the third being the 2017-2028 forecast),
and multi-series line charts (6 with the dual rank/fragility axis, 8, 10, 12).

The chart design is reissued three times with only the country and the y window changed -
0 to 0.8 for Sudan, 0 to 0.6 for Egypt, 0 to 0.6 across the forecast - so a reader
comparing the two case studies has to re-read the axis to see that Sudan's bars and
Egypt's bars are not drawn at the same scale. Figure 8's y window (0 to 0.3) and Figure
10's (0 to 0.25) differ the same way.

Not one figure is multipanel, none shares an axis, none carries a colourbar, none is
three-dimensional. Legends sit below the axes six times, outside on the right once, and
inside the frame never. Printed tick numbers are a clean signal of the figure's job:
present on all seven computed charts, absent from all five schematics.

## Tables
Six tables, two dressings. Tables 1 and 2 have a single rule under the header and no
bottom rule; Tables 3, 4, 5 and 6 are closed frames with a full inner grid. No zebra
anywhere, no diagonal header, no units in a header row, no table turned sideways, none
continued.

Three field-level findings are worth carrying:

- Decimal alignment tracks the data, not the paper. Table 3 prints four places on every
  numeric column and aligns on the point; Table 5 carries the same three measures for the
  same five climatic variables for a different country and does not align, because one
  column mixes 0.04545 with 0.0223.
- Units live in body cells, never in headers. Every cost in Table 6 welds its currency
  word ('50,000,000 dollars'), so the column cannot be summed, and Figure 2 pushes units
  into the flowchart's feature boxes ('% of GNI', 'kt of CO2 equivalent').
- Table 6 is the paper's only merged cell: 'Total Cost' spans both columns and its value
  sits alone on the row beneath.

## What the paper gets wrong, exhibit by exhibit
This is the most self-repeating paper in the lane. The Egypt section reuses the Sudan
section's text and its charts: heading 5.1.2 is still titled 'How Climate change impacts
on fragile Sudan', the lead sentence for Figure 9 still says 'we determine the fragility
of Sudan' inside the Egypt section, and Table 5's caption is word-for-word Table 3's
caption with a different number. None of that is a layout fault and all of it is exactly
what the six field groups are for - a region census would score this paper perfect.

The apparatus has the same character. The variation-coefficient equation on p9 renders
as a smear of overlapping glyphs, unreadable at any zoom. The extractor invents two
phantom section headings on p18 out of Figure 12's axis furniture ('0.45 Before' and
'0.4 After'). A red Chinese resale banner is stamped across the top of every page and
appears nowhere in the text layer. The running folio reads 'Team #89499 Page N of 21' on
a document with 22 physical pages, so the folio is off by one from page 3 onwards. And
welds are everywhere the spacing collapsed: 'Fragilityin the ith year', 'shown in
Figure1', 'indicatorsare shown in Figure 10', 'situation in2028', 'Value0.6',
'SouthSudan', 'CentralAfricanRepublic', 'CongoDemocraticRepublic', 'Table 2Range',
'Table 5Relationship'.
rules: Caption side splits inside one paper: all six table captions print ABOVE their grid and all twelve figure captions print BELOW their art, without a single crossover in 22 pages [caption.position].

The text layer is not a reliable route to caption side here either: Figure 5's caption is emitted in reading order BEFORE the art and the art sits above it, while Figure 6's axis furniture is emitted before the caption line [caption.position].

The caption form is 'Figure <n> <noun phrase>' with no colon and no full stop - the tables use the identical form - so caption style cannot separate a grid from a chart, and two table captions weld their number to the first word ('Table 2Range of three levels', 'Table 5Relationship Index ...') [caption.numbering].
Captions are labels, not sentences: five to twelve words, one sentence each, no unit, no condition, no conclusion and no grammatical verb, in either voice [caption.words].

Five of the seventeen recorded captions name the quantity plotted - 'Fragility of Sudan', 'Fragility of Egypt', 'Variance of Stress, Status and Response Indicators in Egypt', 'Prediction of Fragility in Egypt', 'Fragility in Egypt Before and After Intervention' - and three more name a layer instead of a quantity ('The Theme Layer and Feature Layer of ...') [caption.variable_count].

Twelve of the seventeen pointers use the as-shown-in formula, three name the exhibit directly, and two exhibits carry no pointer at all - Figure 6, whose art prints before its own reading sentence, and Table 1, which no sentence in the paper ever announces [mention.lead_pattern].

Most pointers land on the exhibit's own page: thirteen of seventeen are named on the page the exhibit prints on, two are one page early (Table 4 and Figure 12), one is one page LATE - Figure 1's art is on p5 and its only numbered pointer is on p6, the lane's second negative lead - and one is never named at all (Table 1) [mention.lead_pages].
No exhibit is named twice for a second reading: sixteen of seventeen carry count 1 and Table 1 carries 0, so the paper never returns to an exhibit it has already shown [mention.count].

The pointer sentence is doing the argument's work: 'the fragility of Sudan and the level from 2012 to 2016 as follows' and 'More specifically, the stress indicators, the status indicators, the response indicators are shown in Figure 8' set up the reading before the reader sees a single number [mention.lead_sentence].

Reading sentences come in one shape and stop: a range, a percentage or a rank move, in one clause ('from 2012 to 2015, the change of fragility mainly comes from the change of response indicators as 57.39%') [mention.trail_sentence].

The five diagrams that set the model up - Figures 1 to 5 - are all one family, flowchart-or-schematic, and all five are drawn from the same template: boxed nodes, blue fill, downward arrows, no legend, no numbers, no axes [geometry.family].

Every computed chart is one of only two families: three stacked-bar-plus-line charts (Figures 7, 9 and 11) and four multi-series line charts (Figures 6, 8, 10 and 12). No histogram, scatter, radar, heatmap, box plot, map or pie appears in twelve figures [geometry.family].
Not one of the twelve figures is multipanel: panel_count is 1 throughout, so the paper never composes a grid of axes and never shares an axis between drawings [geometry.panel_count].
Legends are printed below the axes five times, set outside on the right once (Figure 12) and inside the frame never; the five schematics carry no legend at all [geometry.legend].

There is no colourbar, no three-dimensional artwork and no shared axis anywhere in the twelve figures; the only shading that encodes a value is the three-segment stack, and its key is the legend, never a scale [geometry.colorbar].

Printed numbers follow the drawing's job: each of the six recorded computed charts carries tick numbers on both axes and each of the five schematics carries none, so tick numbers mark a chart at a glance [geometry.printed_numbers].

The paper reissues one chart design three times - stacked stress/status/response bars with the fragility series drawn as a line - changing only the country and the y window (0 to 0.8 Sudan, 0 to 0.6 Egypt, 0 to 0.6 forecast), so a reader has to re-read the axis to compare the two case studies [geometry.family].
Two grids are framed and four are open: Tables 3, 4, 5 and 6 are boxed with a full inner grid, Tables 1 and 2 carry a single rule under the header and no bottom rule [table.rule_style].
Zebra striping never appears in six tables, and neither does a diagonal header or a unit printed in a header row: 0 of 6 on all three fields [table.zebra].
Merged cells appear exactly once, in Table 6, where 'Total Cost' spans both columns and its value sits alone on the row below; the other five tables are strictly rectangular [table.merged_cells].

Decimal alignment is a property of the data, not of the paper: Table 3 aligns four places on the point and Table 5, which carries the identical three measures, does not, because one of its columns prints 0.04545 beside 0.0223 [table.decimal_aligned].

Units live in body cells, never in headers: Table 6 welds a currency word to every value ('50,000,000 dollars') and Figure 2's feature boxes print their units inline ('% of GNI', 'kt of CO2 equivalent'), so no column in this paper can be aggregated without text surgery [table.note_sentence].
Five of the six tables are set to the full text measure and only Table 2 shrinks to half of it, so width tracks how much the paper has to say, not how many columns it prints [table.width].
No table is turned sideways, continued across a page break or given a note line; all six are portrait and self-contained [table.orientation].

Size tracks the number of named objects: two columns for a symbol list and a cost sheet, four for five climatic rows against three measures, four for ten ranked countries, two for three fragility bands [table.rows].

The model sections take diagrams and the case-study sections take charts, in that order: all five schematics sit under 3.2.1 and 3.2.2, and every computed exhibit sits under 3.5.1, 3.5.2, 4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.2, 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.2, 6.2 or 6.3 [place.section_kind].

The symbol table is the paper's only exhibit inside the notation section, and it is the one exhibit that reaches backwards: it defines X_ij, Y_ij, P_ij, E_j, g_j, w_j and F_i in section 2.2, and every equation of 3.3 then uses them without a gloss [place.section_path].

Exhibits are spread evenly rather than clustered: eight of the twenty-two pages carry no measured region at all, no page carries three, five pages carry two, and the maximum any single exhibit covers is 0.161 of a page (Table 4) [place.area_frac].

No exhibit owns a page or runs full bleed, and the four chart pages are shared with the prose that reads them: p6, p7, p10, p13 and p15 carry two exhibits each, each pair inside one paragraph [place.page_order].
Document order equals number order for both series - Figures 1 to 12 and Tables 1 to 6 print in sequence - so the paper never has a numbering break, only pointer defects [place.doc_order].

The area figures for vector charts are floors, not measurements: the region pass boxes only the plotting band on Figures 7, 10 and 12 (0.0261, 0.0227 and 0.0118 of the page) while the title, axis labels and legend sit outside the box, so a census that treats region area as exhibit area will report these three charts at a quarter of their true size [place.area_frac].

One printed exhibit has no measured region at all: Figure 8's line chart on p11 is drawn, captioned and pointed at, and the pass returned one region for the page - Figure 7's plotting band - so this paper's census is short by exactly one exhibit [place.doc_order].
